title: Arc 2/5: rename Story to Arc, keeping Story as a resolving alias
summary: The flip itself, atomic with the e2e harness because that gate asserts story.schema.json.
description: Rename the profile type (profile.ts:965), the builtin-template key (template.ts:501) and TYPE_DIRECTORIES (schema.ts:333, Arc -> arcs), retaining Story as a deprecated alias from Arc 1/5. Regenerate .lore/schemas so arc.schema.json replaces story.schema.json. MUST be atomic with docker/e2e/run-e2e.sh: that harness asserts .lore/schemas/story.schema.json parses in three loops (1373, 1413, 1583) plus an rm -f at 1418, and it is a REQUIRED context on dev, so a split would land a red gate. Alias is RESOLVE-ONLY: no story.schema.json is emitted.

acceptanceCriteria.text: profile.ts declares Arc; Story resolves to it as a deprecated alias
TYPE_DIRECTORIES maps Arc to arcs, and the builtin template resolves for Arc

CORRECTED (see note): lore schema export emits arc.schema.json AND RETAINS story.schema.json, and a no-op re-run is byte-identical. As written this criterion said 'prunes story.schema.json', which contradicts the binding ruling (c) recorded on LCLI-552 -- the alias OWNS its slug, so the retained file is owned rather than orphaned. Satisfying the criterion as written would have re-broken the consumers the alias exists to protect.
docker/e2e/run-e2e.sh updated in the SAME commit; the docker e2e harness context is green on the PR head
An existing type: Story document still validates (warning only) and still accepts lore link -- the regression this whole migration exists to prevent
npm run check and lore check both exit 0

ADDED: a deprecated alias resolves EVERYWHERE the canonical name does -- required sections, the query --type filter (both directions), schema export --type, lore types --type -- each proven by running the named command, not a unit test of the predicate beneath it

implementationNotes:
SCOPE UPDATED FROM MEASUREMENT, two changes — one removes work, one adds it.

1. ATOMICITY WITH THE E2E HARNESS IS NO LONGER REQUIRED. Proven rather than inferred, which is what opum-agent asked for. Under ruling (c) the alias owns its slug, so `lore schema export` against an Arc+Story-alias profile emits BOTH arc.schema.json and story.schema.json. Measured against the local build in a scratch bundle: the harness's verbatim assertion form `jq -e . .lore/schemas/<T>.schema.json` passes 6 of 6, and `lore check` reports 0 errors, so the retained file is OWNED rather than orphaned. The three slug loops (run-e2e.sh 1373, 1413, 1583) and the rm -f at 1418 therefore pass UNCHANGED.

SCOPE OF THAT PROOF, kept narrow on purpose and agreed with opum-agent: I measured the specific assertions previously identified as blocking, NOT the full docker harness, which carries far more and is only truly verified when CI runs it. Treat the harness as expected-green, not proven-green.

2. NEW WORK: TYPE_DIRECTORIES NEEDS AN EXPLICIT Arc ENTRY. schema.ts:333 maps Story to "stories" and has no Arc key, so a renamed Arc falls through to the slug fallback and `lore new Story` writes to docs/arc/ — measured, that exact path came back from the local build. Not docs/stories/ (what users have today) and not docs/arcs/ (the plural convention every other built-in type follows: epics, specs, runbooks). The fallback is silent and the path is PUBLIC, so the product-surface rule applies: add `Arc: "arcs"` deliberately rather than inherit docs/arc/ by accident. opum-agent accepted this finding and directed it onto this record rather than leaving it in the message thread.

Open question for whoever executes, NOT decided here: whether `lore new Story` should keep writing to docs/stories/ for continuity, or follow the canonical type to docs/arcs/. Making the directory depend on the spelling used is the confusing option; following the canonical type is the consistent one. lore does not move existing files either way, so this only governs NEW documents.

3. DEPENDENCY: LCLI-558. The alias did not actually preserve link behaviour until LCLI-558 landed (#195) — before it, an un-migrated document resolved to Arc and was then rejected by frontmatter validation. Do not start this task against a dev that predates 5d472eee.

EXECUTED. Three alias-resolution DEFECTS found by doing the flip, all the same mechanism and none of them predicted by this record or LCLI-552.

THE MECHANISM: a raw `profile.types.get(type)` / case-folded string compare against a document's own `type:` spelling. The alias seeds byLowerName and bySlug (LCLI-553), so anything resolving THROUGH those maps inherited it for free -- and anything comparing the raw string did not. LCLI-553 shipped exactly this failure once already (the coupling gate resolved, the validation gate did not, fixed in LCLI-558); these are three more hosts of it. The lesson this record should carry forward for LCLI-555/557: seeding a resolver is not the same as making every reader USE the resolver, and the readers that do not are invisible to any test whose fixtures all use one spelling.

1. REQUIRED SECTIONS -- silently WEAKENED validation. schema.ts requiredSectionsFor did a raw .get(), so `type: Story` yielded [] and every un-migrated document was EXEMPT from the section contract its canonical type declares, while passing every other tier. Measured against the built binary: `type: Story` with no "## Acceptance criteria" exited 0; `type: Arc` identical but for the spelling exited 6. Fixed by resolving through canonicalType. Mutation-tested: reverting the fix reddens exactly 1 of 76 in validate.test.ts, the predicted one.

2. QUERY --type -- silently WRONG ANSWERS, and the worst of the three because it returns 0 hits with exit 0. `lore query --type Story` (a DOCUMENTED CLI example, manifest.ts:822) matched nothing after the rename. The tempting fix -- canonicalize the filter only -- is WORSE than doing nothing: it turns `--type Story` into `Arc` and stops matching the un-migrated `type: Story` documents that are precisely the population the alias exists to serve. Fixed by canonicalizing BOTH sides. Two backends (in-memory and the indexed ladybug reader) funnel through one matchesFilters, so one fix covers both -- verified by reading the call graph, not assumed. Mutation-tested with two mutants: the plain revert reddens 1 (predicted 1); the filter-only mutant reddens 4, where I predicted 2 -- the two I missed also filter `--type Story`, so consistent with the mechanism, but the predicted SUBSET was wrong and is recorded as wrong.

3. expectedResource (template.ts) -- same raw .get(), UNREACHABLE under the built-in profile because its resourceBase is "" and short-circuits first. Fixed anyway rather than left as a known-identical hole, and labelled as such in the comment.

TYPE_DIRECTORIES OPEN QUESTION -- DECIDED: `Arc: "arcs"`, so BOTH spellings scaffold into docs/arcs/. This record left it open between docs/stories/ (continuity) and docs/arcs/ (consistency). Taken as docs/arcs/ because making the output directory depend on the INPUT SPELLING is the confusing option, the alias is an input spelling that is removed at 1.0.0, and lore moves no existing file either way. Measured, not assumed: `lore new Story` writes docs/arcs/<slug>.md with `type: Arc` and Arc's own body template including the managed block. The alias is an input spelling and never an output one.

E2E HARNESS -- the narrow proof held, and MISSED FOUR ASSERTIONS. LCLI-552's note proved the three slug loops pass unchanged under (c) and explicitly scoped itself to "the specific blocking assertions, NOT the full docker harness ... treat as expected-green, not proven-green". That caveat paid: running the real harness found 4 failures the narrow proof could not see -- LCLI-299's scoping assertions hardcode `count == 1` for `--type Story` (now 2 files: arc + its alias) and `count == 7` for the full export (now 8), plus a teardown that removed only story.schema.json and left arc.schema.json, so the rmdir failed. Also fixed: three `lore check docs/stories` sites that silently began checking a directory that no longer exists -- now derived with `STORY_DIR="$(dirname "$STORY_PATH")"` so a future directory change cannot repeat it. The harness deliberately KEEPS saying `lore new Story`, which makes it an end-to-end regression test that the deprecated spelling still works against real binaries.

RAN, not inferred (all against the locally built binary / real containers):
  docker e2e harness   383 passed, 0 failed, exit 0  (was 376/4 before the harness fix)
  bun test             3336 pass, 0 fail, 1 skip     (was 3296 pass / 33 fail at the flip)
  lore check           80 files, 0 errors, 0 warnings, exit 0
  typecheck / lint / lint:shell / check:packages   all exit 0 (lint's 3 warnings are pre-existing, confirmed against a stashed tree)
  lore link three-way  aliased Story doc links (exit 0, id appended, tracker back-ref written); Arc control identical; unknown type still refused at the coupling gate with nothing written to doc or tracker
  schema no-op re-run  byte-identical (sha256 over the whole directory, before and after)

NOT DONE HERE, deliberately: the 22 published text sites still say Story/Task (LCLI-555) -- including the `lore link` hint "(the built-in Story type)" that the negative control above prints verbatim -- and the 12 docs/ documents still carry `type: Story` (LCLI-557), which is exactly why lore check stays at 0 warnings: the alias resolves them.
